items.X_desc: The objects, constraints, and defined terms the post reasons about are the ones the problem specifies, used with the meanings given there. Test: check each condition in the statement against the way the post uses it. Score 1.0 when every stated condition and defined term is used faithfully, 0.5 when one condition is applied loosely or a defined term drifts slightly, 0.0 when a constraint is dropped, a defined term is given a different meaning, or the reasoning is about a different object than the one specified, and NA when the post reasons about nothing.
items.Y_name: Symbols defined before they are used
items.Y_desc: Every symbol and object, including ones the post coins for itself, is defined at or before its first appearance. Test: read forward and flag any symbol whose meaning is not yet fixed when it is first used. Score 1.0 when nothing appears undefined, 0.5 when one symbol's meaning is fixed only by later context but is recoverable, 0.0 when a symbol carrying real weight is never defined, and NA when the post uses no symbols of its own.

items.X_desc: When the argument divides into cases, the post states what the division is over and the listed cases together cover every possibility. Test: name the splitting quantity and check whether the listed cases exhaust its range. Score 1.0 when the principle of division is stated and coverage is complete, 0.5 when coverage is complete but the principle is left implicit, 0.0 when some possibility falls outside every listed case, and NA when the argument uses no case division.
items.Y_desc: The cases are arranged so that near-identical work is not done twice: symmetric cases are reduced to one another and shared reasoning is factored out rather than rewritten. Test: compare the cases and see whether any two run essentially the same argument. Score 1.0 when repetition is factored out or waived by an explicit symmetry, 0.5 when some repetition survives but each case still contributes something, 0.0 when the same reasoning is rerun across cases with no consolidation, and NA when the argument uses no case division.

items.X_desc: The final claim covers everything the question demands: every labelled part, both directions of a characterization, both the construction and the bound for an extremal quantity, and the answer in the form requested. Test: list what the question asks for and check each item against the post's conclusion. Score 1.0 when every demand is met, 0.5 when one part or one direction is handled and the rest is asserted or omitted, 0.0 when the post concludes something other than what was asked, and NA when the post reaches no conclusion.
items.Y_name: A substantive attempt at the demand
items.Y_desc: The post tries to establish the requested result, rather than asking a question, offering a remark, reporting that a solution exists without giving it, or supplying a bare answer. Test: is there reasoning aimed at what the problem demands? Score 1.0 when the post is a substantive attempt, 0.5 when it supplies a real fragment such as a proved lemma or a partial derivation, 0.0 when it is a question, a comment, an unsupported answer, or a claim of having solved the problem, and NA only when the text is empty or unreadable.

items.X_desc: The post identifies what makes the problem hard, or where the real content of the argument sits, instead of treating every step as equally weighted. Test: does any sentence single out the crux, the trap, the bad configuration, or the step at which the hypothesis finally bites? Score 1.0 when the difficulty is named and the argument then attacks it, 0.5 when the emphasis is visible only in how effort is allocated, 0.0 when nothing distinguishes the hard step from the routine ones, and NA when the post advances no argument.
items.Y_name: Care is spent where the difficulty is
items.Y_desc: Care is distributed toward the hard steps: routine manipulation is dispatched quickly while the substantive step receives real attention. Test: compare the treatment of the hardest step with the treatment of the most routine one. Score 1.0 when the hard step gets the most careful treatment, 0.5 when care is spread evenly across steps of unequal difficulty, 0.0 when routine steps are expanded while the substantive one is compressed to an assertion, and NA when all steps are of comparable difficulty.

items.X_name: Decisive reason extractable in one sentence
items.X_desc: After one reading, the reason the argument works can be stated in a single sentence: the invariant, the bijection, the substitution, the auxiliary object, or the inequality that does the work. Test: try to write that sentence using only the post's own words. Score 1.0 when the post foregrounds the decisive step so that sentence writes itself, 0.5 when the reason is genuinely present but must be reconstructed from the steps, 0.0 when the post is a sequence of moves from which no single reason can be extracted, and NA when the post advances no argument.
items.Y_desc: The post says something about why the decisive move was tried: what in the problem suggests it, what an alternative would have cost, or how the idea was reached. Test: is there a statement of reason attached to the non-obvious step, as distinct from the step itself? Score 1.0 when the key move carries a reason a reader could reuse, 0.5 when motivation is offered only in general terms or only for a routine step, 0.0 when every move arrives with no reason attached, and NA when the post advances no argument.

items.X_desc: Material that neither states, supports, nor interprets the mathematics - verbatim restatement of the problem, commentary on the writer's mood or circumstances, praise or complaint about the problem - does not displace the argument. Test: remove the non-mathematical passages and ask whether anything of substance was lost. Score 1.0 when essentially all content does mathematical work, 0.5 when a brief aside precedes an otherwise complete argument, 0.0 when a reader must hunt for the argument among material that does no work, and NA when the post contains no mathematics.
items.Y_desc: The post stands on its own: knowing what is claimed, corrected, or continued does not require reading someone else's contribution. Test: cover everything outside this post and ask whether the argument still has a subject and a conclusion. Score 1.0 when the post is complete in itself, 0.5 when it refers to the surrounding discussion but its own argument remains fully readable, 0.0 when the content is unintelligible without material that is not shown, and NA when the post makes no mathematical statement.

items.X_desc: Each assertion follows from the problem's hypotheses, an earlier assertion, or a stated result, and nothing in the chain presupposes the conclusion. Test: walk the assertions in order and try to name the support for each one. Score 1.0 when every link has visible support, 0.5 when one non-central link lacks support but is easily recoverable, 0.0 when a link has no support at all, depends on what is being proved, or the reasoning is circular, and NA when the post makes no chain of assertions.
items.Y_desc: Stated confidence corresponds to the support given: doubt is attached to the specific step in doubt, well-supported steps are asserted plainly, and unproved assumptions are flagged as assumptions. Test: compare each hedge and each flat assertion with the support the post provides for it. Score 1.0 when confidence and support align throughout, 0.5 when hedging is unlocalized or a supported step is over-qualified, 0.0 when an unsupported step is asserted flatly or the whole post is hedged so that nothing is claimed, and NA when the post makes no claim.

items.X_desc: When the post replaces the stated problem with an easier or equivalent one, it says so and indicates why the replacement is legitimate. Test: locate the sentence performing the swap and check whether the equivalence, or the one direction of implication that suffices, is stated. Score 1.0 when both the reduction and its legitimacy are explicit, 0.5 when the reduction is announced but its legitimacy is left silent, 0.0 when the post silently begins solving a different question, and NA when the post attacks the problem as stated.
items.Y_name: Reductions by symmetry or scaling are licensed
items.Y_desc: Reductions by symmetry, relabelling, scaling, or fixing a value are justified where made, and any scaling is undone before the final answer. Test: for each such reduction check that the symmetry invoked actually exists, and that the reported quantity is expressed in the original terms. Score 1.0 when each reduction is licensed and any rescaling is reversed, 0.5 when a legitimate reduction is asserted without justification, 0.0 when the reduction destroys generality or a scaled quantity is reported as the final answer, and NA when the post makes no such reduction.

items.X_name: General claims are argued, not sampled
items.X_desc: A claim about all members of an unbounded family is established by argument rather than by checking instances and asserting the pattern. Score 1.0 when the argument is carried out for an arbitrary member, 0.5 when it is written for a representative instance but visibly transfers, 0.0 when instances are checked and the general claim is asserted from them, and NA when the claim concerns only finitely many objects that are all treated.

Test: pair every claim, lemma, or we-will-show with the passage that discharges it. Score 1.0 when every stated claim is discharged and the pairing is unambiguous, 0.5 when a claim's proof is present but its boundaries are unclear, 0.0 when a claim is stated and never returned to, and NA when the post states no claims of its own.

items.Y_name: Notation stable and consistent with the statement
items.Y_desc: Symbols taken from the statement keep the meanings given there, any new notation is distinct from them, and each letter carries one meaning throughout. Test: check whether a letter from the statement is silently reassigned and whether any letter serves two roles. Score 1.0 when the statement's notation is respected and new notation is stable, 0.5 when a minor clash or drift costs the reader a translation step, 0.0 when a statement symbol is rebound or one letter denotes two different things, and NA when the post uses no notation.

Test: follow the first substantive step forward and check whether that same line terminates in a stated conclusion. Score 1.0 when a single line runs through to a conclusion, 0.5 when a conclusion is reached only after an unresolved detour or an unexplained switch of method, 0.0 when the line is abandoned or the post breaks off mid-argument, and NA when no line of attack is begun.
items.Y_desc: The computations shown agree with each other and with their own inputs: intermediate quantities are carried forward correctly and the final assembly uses the values the earlier steps produced. Test: recompute two or three transitions and check the last line against the quantities feeding it. Score 1.0 when the visible algebra and arithmetic hold together, 0.5 when a slip appears in a step that does not affect the conclusion, 0.0 when a step does not follow from its inputs or the final assembly contradicts them, and NA when the post displays no computation.

Test: trace the stated answer back to the steps producing it. Score 1.0 when the answer is derived by the reasoning on the page, 0.5 when it is derived but one step of that derivation is skipped, 0.0 when it is announced without derivation, guessed, or obtained by exploiting the listed options or the expected answer format, and NA when the problem asks for a proof rather than a value.

Score 1.0 when every application is licensed by conditions already in evidence, 0.5 when a condition holds but goes unremarked in a place where it is not automatic, 0.0 when a result is applied outside the situation it governs, and NA when the post applies no named result.
items.Y_desc: For each variable it is clear whether it is arbitrary, chosen, universally quantified, or fixed, and that status does not change without notice. Test: for each variable find where it is bound and check that later uses respect that binding. Score 1.0 when every variable's status is unambiguous throughout, 0.5 when one binding must be inferred from context but is recoverable, 0.0 when a variable's role changes mid-argument or the scope of a claim cannot be determined, and NA when the post introduces no variables.

items.X_name: Applied results have their conditions in evidence
items.X_desc: When the post applies a named result, the conditions that result requires are either verified or plainly satisfied by the objects at hand. Test: for each application, ask whether the required conditions have been established for the specific objects used. Score 1.0 when every application is licensed by conditions already in evidence, 0.5 when a condition holds but goes unremarked in a place where it is not automatic, 0.0 when a result is applied outside the situation it governs, and NA when the post applies no named result.
items.Y_desc: The computations shown agree with each other and with their own inputs: intermediate quantities are carried forward correctly and the final assembly uses the values the earlier steps produced. Test: recompute two or three transitions and check the last line against the quantities feeding it. Score 1.0 when the visible algebra and arithmetic hold together, 0.5 when a slip appears in a step that does not affect the conclusion, 0.0 when a step does not follow from its inputs or the final assembly contradicts them, and NA when the post displays no computation.

items.X_name: Exposed edge and equality cases are treated
items.X_desc: Boundary values, degenerate instances, small parameters, and equality conditions that the argument's own steps expose are addressed rather than passed over. Test: look for division by a possibly zero quantity, an inequality used at equality, extreme parameter values, and configurations the construction may not cover. Score 1.0 when the exposed situations are treated, 0.5 when they are noticed but dismissed without argument, 0.0 when a step silently assumes such a case away, and NA when the argument's own steps expose no such situation.
items.Y_desc: Statements the post presents as claims or lemmas are argued rather than left standing, and each argued block makes clear which statement it settles. Test: pair every claim, lemma, or we-will-show with the passage that discharges it. Score 1.0 when every stated claim is discharged and the pairing is unambiguous, 0.5 when a claim's proof is present but its boundaries are unclear, 0.0 when a claim is stated and never returned to, and NA when the post states no claims of its own.

items.X_desc: Each assertion follows from the problem's hypotheses, an earlier assertion, or a stated result, and nothing in the chain presupposes the conclusion. Test: walk the assertions in order and try to name the support for each one. Score 1.0 when every link has visible support, 0.5 when one non-central link lacks support but is easily recoverable, 0.0 when a link has no support at all, depends on what is being proved, or the reasoning is circular, and NA when the post makes no chain of assertions.

anchors.X_name: The route is announced before the algebra
anchors.X_desc: Whether the post says what method it is about to use before it starts computing.
anchors.Y_desc: Whether the reader is told the intended line of attack before the technical work begins.

anchors.X_name: Notation is introduced before it is used
anchors.X_desc: Whether every symbol the post uses is defined at or before its first appearance.
anchors.Y_desc: Whether the reader is told what each letter stands for before it appears in an expression.

anchors.X_desc: Whether the post says what makes the problem hard and what its central move exists to defeat.
anchors.Y_desc: How many display-math blocks the post contains.

anchors.X_desc: Whether the post verifies that the conditions a cited theorem needs actually hold here.
anchors.Y_desc: How many words the post runs to.
